newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia to seek back debts from Libya, Iraq-Chubais.
newsitem.headline: Russia to seek back debts from Libya, Iraq-Chubais.

text.p: Russia plans to step up efforts to get nations including Libya and Iraq to pay off their debts, First Deputy Prime Minister Anatoly Chubais said on Thursday.

"Were working on the question. It's not normal to take a passive position in the current international context," Chubais told a meeting of a presidential advisory council. "It's too big a luxury to forget about those enormous debts."
Chubais, who oversees Russian economic policy and is also Finance Minister, named Libya and Iraq as large debtors, which owe $2.5 billion and $7 billion respectively.
Overall, Russia is seeking repayment of about $37 billion it is owed mainly by developing countries.

Moscow is hoping that membership in the Paris Club of creditor nations, which it hopes to obtain later this month, will help it negotiate debt owned by former allies of the Soviet Union. But in any case the talks are likely to be complex as most of the debt was taken out in roubles many years ago.
As a debtor Russia signed a $40 billion rescheduling agreement with the Paris Club for 25 years in 1995.
Chubais also told the meeting he expected commercial bank interest rates to fall to 20 percent in 1998.
"We guarantee, provided that the government continues its economic policies, that annual interest rates will fall to 20 percent in 1998," he said.
Average interest rates on bank credits are now 45 percent, down from 61 percent at the start of the year, a senior central bank official, Mikhail Sukhov, said earlier on Thursday.
Chubais said Russia's monthly inflation rate was one percent in May, and said he expected lower rates in June and July.
But the situation with unpaid government wages to soldiers and officials was "critical", Chubais said, and he promised to work out a schedule of payments within three days.
